properties.description: Copper oxide array on carbon fiber
Nickel deposited on copper array on carbon fiber

nodes.name: Cu foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Copper foam (CF) was in turn washed with 3 M HCl solution and absolute ethanol under the ultrasonic assistance to remove impurities on the surface.
nodes.source_text: First, copper foam (CF) was in turn washed with 3 M HCl solution and absolute ethanol under the ultrasonic assistance to remove impurities on the surface.

nodes.name: Electrochemical oxidation to CuO array
nodes.procedure: A piece of CF with the size of 1.0 × 1.0 cm² was used as the working electrode and a platinum wire (or carbon rod) as the counter electrode. The electrochemical oxidation was carried out in 3 M NaOH solution at 70 °C for 20 min at a current density of 50 mA cm⁻². The color of CF changed from yellow to black.

unit_operations.name: Electrochemical oxidation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The electrochemical oxidation was carried out in 3 M NaOH solution at 70 °C for 20 min at a current density of 50 mA cm⁻².

nodes.source_text: The electrochemical oxidation was carried out in 3 M NaOH solution at 70 °C for 20 min at a current density of 50 mA cm⁻².

nodes.name: Electrochemical reduction to Cu array
nodes.procedure: After the above black CF electrode had been removed from NaOH solution and rinsed with deionized water, it was electrochemically reduced in 1 M Na₂SO₄ solution at ambient temperature for 30 min at the current density of -50 mA cm⁻² [31]. Here, the color of CF changed from black to reddish brown. Thus, the grasslike Cu nanosheet array/CF electrode (labeled as Cu/CF) was prepared.

unit_operations.name: Electrochemical reduction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: it was electrochemically reduced in 1 M Na₂SO₄ solution at ambient temperature for 30 min at the current density of -50 mA cm⁻².

nodes.source_text: After the above black CF electrode had been removed from NaOH solution and rinsed with deionized water, it was electrochemically reduced in 1 M Na₂SO₄ solution at ambient temperature for 30 min at the current density of -50 mA cm⁻².

nodes.name: Ni electrodeposition on Cu array
nodes.procedure: To obtain grass-like Ni/Cu nanosheet array/CF electrode (labeled as Ni/Cu/CF), the grass-like Cu nanosheet array/CF was used as the working electrode and a 30 mL aqueous solution containing 1.5771 g NiSO₄·6H₂O and 2.6469 g C₆H₅Na₃O₇·2H₂O as the electrolyte, in which the pH was 5.97. In the above same two-electrode system, metallic Ni was deposited on the Cu/CF at a current density of -50 mA cm⁻² under quiescent conditions at room temperature for 20 min.

unit_operations.name: Ni electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: metallic Ni was deposited on the Cu/CF at a current density of -50 mA cm⁻² under quiescent conditions at room temperature for 20 min.

nodes.source_text: metallic Ni was deposited on the Cu/CF at a current density of -50 mA cm⁻² under quiescent conditions at room temperature for 20 min.

nodes.name: Control Ni/CF preparation
nodes.procedure: As a control, the Ni/CF electrode was also prepared in the above 30 mL aqueous solution containing 1.5771 g NiSO₄·6H₂O and 2.6469 g C₆H₅Na₃O₇·2H₂O under the same deposition conditions, employing CF as the working electrode.
nodes.source_text: the Ni/CF electrode was also prepared in the above 30 mL aqueous solution containing 1.5771 g NiSO₄·6H₂O and 2.6469 g C₆H₅Na₃O₇·2H₂O under the same deposition conditions, employing CF as the working electrode.

nodes.description: HER LSV performance in 1 M KOH (comparative testing of multiple catalysts)
nodes.source_text: The HER linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) polarization curve with 85 % iR compensation was recorded at the scan rate of 1 mV s-1... Only the overpotential of 38 mV was demanded to gain the current density of -10 mA cm-2. Even at the current density of -50 mA cm-2, the overpotential was merely 103 mV.

nodes.description: HER chronopotentiometry stability at -30 mA/cm² in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: A 50 h stability test was performed using chronopotentiometry at a current density of -30 mA cm-2 without iR compensation... After continuously catalyzing for 50 h, the overpotential change is merely 25 mV.

nodes.description: HER CV cycle stability (1000 cycles) in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: LSV curves of the Ni/Cu/CF electrode before and after 1000 CV cycles in 1 M KOH... the overpotential hardly increases after 1000 cycles.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting LSV in two-electrode setup with RuO2/CF anode
nodes.source_text: the Ni/Cu/CF // RuO2/CF electrode only needed a cell voltage of 1.51 V to reach a current density of 10 mA cm-2.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting chronopotentiometry stability and Faradaic efficiency
nodes.source_text: Continuously catalyzing for 50 h, the chronopotentiometry curve... hardly changes... Faradaic efficiency of ~100 %.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of the final Ni/Cu product displays diffraction peaks of metallic Cu and Ni (Fig.2c).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The successful loading of Ni on Cu nanosheet array was also proven by XRD analysis (Fig.2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM images show Ni/Cu array/CF with nanosheet thickness increased to 30-40 nm and pores disappeared (Fig.1e).
nodes.evidence_snippet: After metallic Ni was deposited on Cu nanosheet array, the thickness of the nanosheets increased to 30~40 nm and the pores disappeared (see Fig.1e).

properties.features: porous, nanofibrous morphology with high surface area structure

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ni/Cu nanosheet with rough edge and increased thickness, pores disappeared after Ni deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After Ni is deposited, the pores disappear; and the edge of the nanosheet becomes rough. Simultaneously, the thickness of the nanosheet markedly increases (see Fig.3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/Cu nanosheet array owned the BET surface area of 10.81 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Here, the N₂ adsorption-desorption experiments showed that as-obtained Ni/Cu nanosheet array owned the BET surface area of 10.81 m² g⁻¹ (see Fig.S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS shows Cu and Ni element peaks clearly visible with uniform distributions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig.4a, Cu and Ni element peaks are clearly visible. Fig.4b exhibits the EDS mapping images of Cu and Ni, from which one can readily see the uniform distributions of Cu and Ni elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows Cu, Ni, C, O peaks; Cu 2p: 931.2/952.0 eV (Cu⁰), 933.8/953.8 eV (Cu²⁺, weaker); Ni 2p: 852.3/869.6 eV (Ni⁰), 855.6/873.3 eV (Ni²⁺, stronger).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figs.5b,c show the high-resolution XPS spectra of Cu 2p and Ni2p, respectively. In Cu 2p XPS spectrum... four peaks are detected... In Ni 2p XPS spectrum, six peaks can be clearly seen.

properties.description: High-resolution XPS spectrum showing core level peaks

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Ni atomic percentage in Ni/Cu catalyst from 3.8%-20.7% with deposition time.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-OES analyses uncovered that the atomic percentage of Ni in the final catalyst increased from 3.8%-20.7% with prolonging the deposition time from 5 to 25 min (see Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region gives Cdl = 70.0 mF cm⁻² for Ni/Cu/CF (ECSA = 1750 cm²) vs 20.9 mF cm⁻² for Ni/CF (ECSA = 522.5 cm²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl is 70.0 mF cm⁻² for the Ni/Cu/CF electrode and 20.9 mF cm⁻² for the Ni/CF one, respectively. The ECSA values of two electrodes are calculated to be 1750 and 522.5 cm².
